clue.text: Provision for borrowing one pound in financial centre with nothing up front

indicators.note: the nothing comes first in the answer

parts.note: sweet FA is slang for nothing at all

indicators.note: the one and the pound sit inside the financial centre

parts.note: the City is London's financial district
I is the Roman numeral for one
L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A loan arrangement in the City for a single pound, with no deposit paid upfront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing up front' puts FA before C(IL)ITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A credit facility is an arrangement by which a bank lets a customer borrow money.

clue.text: Device to avoid duties that's bog standard?

explanation.surface: A tax dodge is mocked as something utterly mediocre.
explanation.walkthrough: Bog-standard means ordinary, but here a bog is a toilet (a convenience) and a standard is a flag, so a flag of convenience is a standard of the bog.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipowners register vessels under a foreign registry to escape taxes and regulations; read literally, a toilet's banner.

clue.text: See 1
Nigella Lawson's TV programme

indicators.note: the possessive 's reads as 'has', so the name has the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A cookery presenter's television show is named.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigella Lawson presents food shows; but split NIGEL LA LAW SON and the American legal drama sits in her name.
explanation.definitionFit: The series was a long-running American drama about a Los Angeles law firm.

clue.text: TV programme — Baron, not mother, could be this

indicators.note: the letters of the three words could be rearranged into the programme's title

explanation.surface: A sitcom title is linked to a nobleman who is not anyone's mum.
explanation.walkthrough: A 1970s British sitcom about a widow forced to sell her manor house. 'Baron, not mother' is the fodder, so 'not' supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This BBC sitcom starred Penelope Keith as an aristocratic widow living in her old estate's lodge.

clue.text: Odd characters in ancient piece like vinegar

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Some antique object is said to resemble vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegar is a dilute solution of the acid named after the Latin for vinegar, acetum.

clue.text: Tipple getting a neurotic drunk

indicators.note: being drunk leaves the letters of the phrase scrambled

explanation.surface: An anxious person has a drink and gets drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: This orange-flavoured French liqueur is a drink, a tipple.

clue.text: Boat turning belly up

indicators.note: turning, with up in a down clue, has the word for belly read bottom to top

parts.note: gut is another word for belly

explanation.surface: A vessel capsizes so that its underside faces the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A small powerful vessel that pulls or pushes larger ships is a type of boat.

clue.text: Coping with international's character

parts.note: an international player wins a cap, so the international's is cap's
tone is a quality or character, as in the tone of a place

explanation.surface: Dealing with the personality of a sportsman who plays for his country.
explanation.walkthrough: Coping is the top course of a wall, not managing.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstone is a stone in the top layer of a wall, which is called its coping.

clue.text: Rooney's Portuguese World Cup opponent could be such an enthusiast

definitions.text: Rooney's Portuguese World Cup opponent could be such an enthusiast

parts.words: Rooney's Portuguese World Cup opponent could be such an enthusiast
parts.note: in 2006 Wayne Rooney was sent off for treading on Ricardo Carvalho of Portugal, who thus received a heavy tread from a boot

explanation.surface: A footballer's opponent is imagined as a hobbyist.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 2006 World Cup quarter-final England's Wayne Rooney stamped on Portugal's Ricardo Carvalho, so the Portuguese player gathered a stamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A philatelist, someone who gathers postage issues as a hobby, is also someone who received a stamp.

clue.text: Girl left record

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl departed and set a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Annals are historical records kept year by year; the singular is one such record.

clue.text: Accumulating rubbish collection on horse

parts.note: totting is British slang for scavenging saleable items from rubbish
a rider on horseback is said to be up

explanation.surface: Someone gathering refuse rides a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: A totter is a rag-and-bone collector of old junk; a jockey is 'up' when mounted.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding figures together into a running total is a way of building up a sum.

clue.text: However eccentric, Lord Mayor is best

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: LM is an abbreviation for Lord Mayor

explanation.surface: A Lord Mayor, however odd, is the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best' is a verb here, to defeat, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat them, to swamp or crush them completely.

clue.text: Entice military police in Vietnam offensive

indicators.note: the police go inside the offensive

parts.note: the Tet offensive of 1968 was a major Vietnam War campaign

explanation.surface: Soldiers' police lure people during a wartime campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or seduce someone into doing something.

clue.text: What gives victory for striker over director

indicators.note: in a down clue the striker goes above the director

parts.note: a match is struck to light it, so it is a striker
Michael Winner was a British film director

explanation.surface: A goalscorer is credited ahead of the manager for a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' and 'director' suggest football roles, but they are a match and the film director Michael Winner.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive goal or player that secures a win for a side.

clue.text: He accounted for reactions as in third of laws

definitions.text: He accounted for reactions as in third of laws

indicators.note: accounted for suggests the letters are explained by being reordered into a name
the third letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: The physicist who explained reactions in his third law.
explanation.walkthrough: Newton's third law states that every action has an equal and opposite reaction; the anagram of REACTIONS AS IN plus W from 'laws' gives his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist who formulated three laws of motion, the third concerning action and reaction.

clue.text: One maligns key people

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
slanders means speaks ill of, maligns

explanation.surface: Someone badmouths important people.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is a small low island, so its inhabitants are people of an island.

clue.text: Held in muscles, rounded

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles
orbed means made round, like an orb

explanation.surface: Something was contained by bulging muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid soaked up and retained by a sponge has been taken in and kept.

clue.text: Should be fun galore — not half crazy

definitions.text: Should be fun galore — not half crazy

indicators.note: crazy means the combined letters are jumbled
only the first half of the word is kept, the rest dropped

explanation.surface: Something promises plenty of fun, or wild nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'galore — not half' leaves GAL, which joins SHOULD BE FUN in the anagram; 'not half' also suggests 'very much', the surface's slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A very entertaining person or thing, which a lot of fun ought to be.

clue.text: African with range of knowledge about New York area

indicators.note: the range of knowledge goes round the other letters

parts.note: ken is one's range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: An African with wide knowledge of the New York district.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Kenya, a country in East Africa.

clue.text: One of seven — or eleven or twelve?

definitions.text: One of seven — or eleven or twelve?

parts.words: One of seven — or eleven or twelve?
parts.note: one of the seven seas, and the name before Eleven and Twelve in the heist film titles

explanation.surface: A puzzle over which of a group of numbers something belongs to.
explanation.walkthrough: There are said to be seven seas, and the George Clooney heist films are Ocean's Eleven and Ocean's Twelve.
explanation.definitionFit: A great body of salt water, one of the world's seas; also the surname in the heist films.

clue.text: I'd enable beggar finally to get stuffing

definitions.text: I'd enable beggar finally to get stuffing

indicators.note: stuffing suggests the letters are crammed together in a new order
the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone offers to help a pauper finally get food.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of I'D ENABLE with R from 'beggar' gives the answer, and the whole clue describes what a food queue does for the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: The breadline is the level of poverty at which people depend on handouts of food.

clue.text: Material study supported by Institute of Management

indicators.note: in a down clue the study sits on top of the institute

parts.note: a den is a private room for study
IM is short for Institute of Management

explanation.surface: A management college backs a piece of research.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-wearing cotton twill used for jeans is a fabric.

clue.text: Rodent clubbed without state resistance

indicators.note: without means outside, so the clubbed word goes round the rest

parts.note: beat means struck, clubbed
aver means to state or assert
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A rodent was clubbed without the state resisting.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australian water rodent is a species of rat.

clue.text: A success in time past

parts.note: a go is a success, as in make a go of it

explanation.surface: A triumph in earlier days.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago means before now, as in years back.

clue.text: Dimwit finding place to stay in city

indicators.note: the inn goes inside the city

parts.note: NY is New York, a city
an inn is a place to stay overnight

explanation.surface: A fool finds lodgings in town.
explanation.definitionFit: A foolish, silly person is a nitwit.

clue.text: Medicine unknown morbid condition needed

parts.note: drops are liquid medicine
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An unknown remedy is needed for an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedema, swelling caused by fluid in the tissues, is an old name for a disease.

clue.text: Decorate sort of knitwear for a craft

parts.note: trim means to decorate or adorn
Aran is a style of chunky knitwear from the Aran Islands

explanation.surface: Someone embellishes a jumper for a handicraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like handicraft, but it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing vessel with three hulls is a type of boat.
